# teams app create

Create a new Teams app with bot

## Usage

```
teams app create [options]
```

## Options

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `-n, --name <name>` | App/bot name |
| `-e, --endpoint <url>` | [OPTIONAL] Messaging endpoint URL |
| `--messaging-mode <mode>` | [OPTIONAL] How Teams delivers messages: socket or http |
| `--env <path>` | [OPTIONAL] Path to credentials file (.env or appsettings.json) |
| `--env-file <path>` | [OPTIONAL] Alias for --env |
| `--no-secret` | [OPTIONAL] Skip client secret generation (for managed identity or federated credentials) |
| `--azure` | [OPTIONAL] Create bot in Azure (requires az CLI) |
| `--teams-managed` | [OPTIONAL] Create bot managed by Teams (default) |
| `--service-management-reference <id>` | [OPTIONAL] ServiceTree service ID for Microsoft Entra app attribution |
| `--sign-in-audience <audience>` | [OPTIONAL] Microsoft Entra sign-in audience: myOrg or multipleOrgs |
| `--subscription <id>` | [OPTIONAL] Azure subscription ID (defaults to az CLI default) |
| `--resource-group <name>` | Azure resource group (required for --azure) |
| `--create-resource-group` | [OPTIONAL] Create the resource group if it doesn't exist |
| `--region <name>` | [OPTIONAL] Azure region for resource group (default: westus2) |
| `--color-icon <path>` | [OPTIONAL] Path to color icon (192x192 PNG) |
| `--outline-icon <path>` | [OPTIONAL] Path to outline icon (32x32 PNG) |
| `--json` | [OPTIONAL] Output as JSON |
<!-- AUTOGENERATED:END -->

## Details

Creates a complete Teams bot app in a single command: AAD app registration, client secret, manifest, Teams app import, and bot registration.

### Manifest Version

New apps use manifest schema version **1.30**. The generated `manifestVersion` and `$schema` URL use the same pinned version, updated with CLI releases rather than discovered through an API. Existing apps and their manifest versions are not changed.

### Bot Location

By default, the bot is Teams-managed (no Azure subscription needed). Use `--azure` to create an Azure Bot instead, which is required for OAuth and SSO features.

**Precedence:** `--azure`/`--teams-managed` flag > `teams config set default-bot-location` > Teams-managed default.

See [Bot Locations](../../concepts/bot-locations) for details on the trade-offs.

### Messaging Mode

Use `--messaging-mode socket` to receive messages without a public HTTP endpoint or tunnel:

```bash
teams app create --name "My Bot" --messaging-mode socket
```

The CLI configures socket mode for both Teams-managed and Azure bots. Interactive creation offers a messaging-mode choice; scripted creation keeps HTTP mode unless socket mode is requested. `--messaging-mode socket` cannot be combined with `--endpoint`.

Create a Teams-managed socket-mode bot and save its credentials:

```bash
teams app create --name "My Bot" --teams-managed --messaging-mode socket --env .env
```

For an Azure bot, use the same mode flag with your Azure resource options. Azure CLI must be installed and logged in:

```bash
teams app create --name "My Azure Bot" --azure --subscription <id> --resource-group my-rg --messaging-mode socket --env .env
```

Socket mode changes message delivery, not where the bot is registered. It does not start your bot application; run your Teams SDK application with the generated credentials.

Socket mode is currently available only for new bots.

Socket-mode configuration requires the caller to be an owner of the bot's Entra app. For service-attributed apps, verify ownership if enabling socket mode fails.

If enabling socket mode fails, creation still succeeds and the bot falls back to HTTP mode. The app and bot still exist; do not create them again. No messaging endpoint is configured when creating with `--messaging-mode socket`, so HTTP delivery requires setting a public HTTPS endpoint:

```bash
teams app update <teamsAppId> --messaging-mode http --endpoint https://mybot.azurewebsites.net/api/messages
```

The CLI prints a retry hint. JSON output includes `socketMode: false` and `socketModeError` in that case. To retry socket mode instead, use the returned `teamsAppId`, then verify the mode:

```bash
teams app update <teamsAppId> --messaging-mode socket
teams app get <teamsAppId> --json
```

Successful socket-mode creation reports `socketMode: true` in JSON. See [app update](./update#messaging-mode) to switch back to HTTP.

### Scopes

During interactive creation, you can customize which scopes the bot supports:

| Scope | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **Personal** | 1:1 chat with the bot (default) |
| **Team** | Channel conversations (default) |
| **Group Chat** | Group chat conversations (default) |
| **Copilot** | Available as a custom engine agent in M365 Copilot |

Selecting **Copilot** automatically adds the `copilotAgents.customEngineAgents` block to the manifest and ensures the **Personal** scope is included (required by M365 Copilot).

The built-in **Chat** (`conversations`) and **About** tabs are added only when **Personal** scope is enabled. Team-only and group-chat-only bots do not get personal tabs.

### Channel Compatibility

New apps include `supportsChannelFeatures: "tier1"` to declare support across all channel types. To add this declaration to an existing app after confirming compatibility:

```bash
teams app manifest update <appId> --set-json 'supportsChannelFeatures="tier1"'
```

Changing bot scopes does not change an existing channel compatibility declaration.

### Examples

Create with defaults (Teams-managed, generated manifest):

```bash
teams app create --name "My Bot"
```

Create with Azure bot and write credentials to `.env`:

```bash
teams app create --name "My Bot" --azure --subscription <id> --resource-group my-rg --env .env
```

For C# projects, write credentials to `appsettings.json` instead:

```bash
teams app create --name "My Bot" --env appsettings.json
```

This writes credentials under a `Teams` section with PascalCase keys (`ClientId`, `ClientSecret`, `TenantId`).

### Skipping Secret Generation

Use `--no-secret` to skip client secret generation when using managed identity or federated credentials:

```bash
teams app create --name "My Bot" --no-secret
```

Only `CLIENT_ID` and `TENANT_ID` are output. You can generate a secret later with [`teams app auth secret create`](./auth-secret-create).

### Service-Attributed Apps

Some tenants require new Microsoft Entra app registrations to be attributed to a service. Use `--service-management-reference` with the ServiceTree service ID, and `--sign-in-audience myOrg` when tenant policy requires a single-tenant app:

```bash
teams app create --name "My Bot" --service-management-reference <service-id> --sign-in-audience myOrg --no-secret
```

### Output

On success, outputs:

```
CLIENT_ID=<app-client-id>
CLIENT_SECRET=<generated-secret>
TENANT_ID=<your-tenant-id>
```

### Portal Equivalent

In the [Teams Developer Portal](https://dev.teams.microsoft.com), this is equivalent to: Apps → New app, then separately configuring bot registration and generating credentials. The CLI does it all in one step.
